## C1. Naturality of the isomorphism `Ext¹(ℤ/k, Y) ≅ Y/kY`

The isomorphism `Ext¹(ℤ/k, Y) ≅ Y/kY` is natural in `Y`: for every morphism `f : Y ⟶ Y'` of
`ℤ`-modules the induced square, with vertical maps the isomorphisms and horizontal maps
`Ext¹(ℤ/k, f)` and the map induced by `f` on the quotients, commutes.

*Status.* The isomorphism itself is a theorem: `extOneZModEquiv` gives `Y ⧸ kY ≃+ Ext¹(ℤ/k, Y)`
for every `k ≠ 0`, built from the explicit surjection `y ↦ extClass ∘ (1 ↦ y)`
(`extOneHom_surjective`) whose kernel is exactly `kY` (`ker_extOneHom`). What is not formalised is
functoriality of this description in `Y`. Falsified by a morphism `f` for which the square fails
to commute.

## C2. Hereditarity of `ℤ`: all `Extⁿ` vanish for `n ≥ 2`

For all `ℤ`-modules `X`, `Y` and all `n : ℕ`, `Extⁿ⁺²(X, Y) = 0`.

*Status.* Now proved in three cases. (i) `Extⁿ⁺²(X, ℤ) = 0` for all `X` (`ext_int_eq_zero`;
injective dimension of `ℤ` is `≤ 1`, and the bundled `intInjectiveResolution` gives `Rⁿ⁺²F(ℤ) = 0`
for every additive `F`). (ii) `Extⁿ⁺²(ℤ/k, Y) = 0` for all `Y` (`ext_zmod_eq_zero`). (iii) More
generally `Extⁿ⁺²(X, Y) = 0` for every **finitely generated** `X` and every `Y`
(`ext_fg_eq_zero`), obtained from the free presentation `0 → ker f → ℤᵐ → X → 0` whose kernel is
again free (`free_ker_of_fin`) via the abstract criterion
`ext_eq_zero_of_projective_presentation`. The remaining case is `X` of infinite rank; it needs the
statement — not currently in Mathlib — that *every* submodule of a free `ℤ`-module is free.
Falsified by a single pair `X`, `Y` with `Ext²(X, Y) ≠ 0`.

## C3. `Tor₁` against the prime cyclic groups already detects flatness

For a `ℤ`-module `G`: `G` is flat if and only if `Tor₁(G, ℤ/p) = 0` for every **prime** `p`.

*Status.* The version quantified over all `k ≠ 0` is now a theorem:
`flat_iff_isZero_torOne_zmod` proves `Flat ℤ G ↔ ∀ k ≠ 0, Tor₁(G, ℤ/k) = 0`, via
`flat_iff_torsionFree` (flat = torsion-free over a Bezout domain),
`isZero_kernel_mulBy_iff` (`ker(k·) = 0` iff `k` acts injectively) and the computation
`torOneZModIso : Tor₁(G, ℤ/k) ≅ G[k]`; the strengthening
`flat_iff_isZero_tor_succ` shows flatness is equivalent to the vanishing of *all* `Torₙ₊₁(G, −)`.
The conjecture asks whether the test family can be shrunk to the primes, i.e. whether
`G[p] = 0` for all primes `p` forces `G[k] = 0` for all `k ≥ 1`. Falsified by a group `G` with
`G[p] = 0` for every prime `p` but `Tor₁(G, ℤ/k) ≠ 0` for some `k`.

## C4. Balancing of `Tor`

For all `ℤ`-modules `G`, `H` and all `n`, the two left-derived functors of the tensor product
agree: `Tor(ModuleCat ℤ) n ≅ Tor'(ModuleCat ℤ) n`, and in particular
`Tor₁(G, H) ≅ Tor₁(H, G)`.

*Status.* Mathlib defines both `Tor` (derived in the second variable) and `Tor'` (derived in the
first) but does not prove them isomorphic. Our computation gives strong evidence in the cyclic
case: `Tor₁(G, ℤ/k) ≅ G[k]` (`torOneZModIso`), which for `G = ℤ/m` has order `gcd(k, m)`,
symmetric in `k` and `m`; and `Torₙ₊₂(G, ℤ/k) = 0` (`isZero_Tor_two_le_zmod`) matches the
vanishing of `Tor'ₙ₊₂` predicted by the same resolution used in the other variable. Falsified by
a pair `G`, `H` and a degree `n` with `Torₙ(G, H) ≇ Tor'ₙ(G, H)`.

## C5. Universal coefficient theorem with the `Tor` correction term

Let `C` be a chain complex of free `ℤ`-modules and `G` an abelian group. Then for every `n` there
is a short exact sequence
`0 → Hₙ(C) ⊗ G → Hₙ(C ⊗ G) → Tor₁(Hₙ₋₁(C), G) → 0`,
natural in `C` and `G`, and split (non-naturally).

*Status.* We proved the theorem for the two-term free complex `C = (ℤ --(·k)--> ℤ)` in both
degrees: `H₀(G ⊗ C) ≅ G ⊗ H₀(C)` (`uctHomologyZeroIso`, no correction term since `H₋₁ = 0`) and
`H₁(G ⊗ C) ≅ Tor₁(G, H₀(C))` (`uctHomologyOneIso`, pure correction term since `H₁(C) = 0`,
`isZero_resComplex_homology_one`); the correction term is genuinely nonzero
(`not_isZero_uct_tor_term`, `torOneZMod_self_ne_zero`). We also proved the flat-coefficient case
`Hₙ(C ⊗ G) ≅ Hₙ(C) ⊗ G` for arbitrary complexes over any commutative ring
(`homologyTensorFlatIso`). Proving the general statement needs freeness of submodules of free
`ℤ`-modules (cf. C2) and the splitting `C ≅ Z ⊕ B[-1]`. Falsified by a free complex `C`, a group
`G` and a degree `n` where the displayed sequence is not exact.
